question: If the accepted D03 model's second two-hour mission is scheduled at hour 24.5 instead of hour 20, so its nominal mission window overlaps the first CAL24 PM window, which activity proceeds and how do the mission, PM and full 60-hour status ledgers reconcile?

manual_rules: OperationProfile.STIM specifies the scheduled mission start within the explicit profile, is part of its key and is in hours by default. For individual fixed missions DTIM is the maximum allowed start delay before cancellation (pages 270-273).
The accepted parent has one CAL24 calendar PM row with a referenced one-hour subtask (pages 387-389); its actual first PM occupies hours 24-25, established by the accepted native run.

source_delta.only_changed_cell: OperationProfile BASIC-SCHEDULE/BASIC-MISSION second row STIM 20.0 to 24.5 hours
retained: First and third missions STIM 8 and 32 hours; MissionType.DURN=2 hours; second mission DTIM=0.3333333333333333 hours
One aircraft, fixed seed 1, one repetition and 60-hour horizon
MaterielPM.PMINT=24 CALHOURS, ATIM=DTIM=0, PMLocation task reference and sole TaskBreakDown.DURN=1 hour
Control.ENPM=Y and all MISSION/SYSTEM half-hour result collection settings
All other authored source cells and all table structure; STIM is part of the native OperationProfile key, so the moved row has a new key identity even though its other field values are retained

Compare stable event prefix only before hour 19, the accepted parent's earliest affected second-mission notification; explain each later divergence without assuming a child prefix through hour 23.5. Do not infer physical stocked items from aggregate PNB.

limits: One fixed seed, one aircraft, a single shifted mission and one calendar PM task at one unit; no general same-time event priority, resource contention, alternate deferment or recurrence rule follows.
The scheduled mission/parent PM windows overlap; actual conflict behavior must be established from native output rather than source timing alone.
